title: Starting up and directing in a scenario
blurb: Place a starting up or directing event in the right activity, workshop and topic, and say who should lead it.
question: Larkspur Rail's board members and agile lead meet in stage 2 to revisit the Agilometer and plan mitigations for risks to agile adoption. Which process and workshop is this, and which topic comes first?

teach.body: Starting up a project asks one question: do we have a viable and worthwhile project? It is triggered by the project mandate, which is whatever information starts the project, such as a feasibility study or, for a supplier, a request for proposal. Directing a project lets the project board stay accountable by making the key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager. In PRINCE2 Agile both processes keep these purposes but gain agile artifacts and named workshops.

head: Activity
What happens in PRINCE2 Agile
rows: The PM creates the daily log
PM reviews similar projects with key stakeholders; lessons log if needed
Executive leads the project canvas from the mandate; PM, CPO, senior supplier and executive create the project backlog
Evaluate delivery options; note tailoring needs if known
Objectives, scope, exclusions, tolerances, constraints, assumptions, dependencies
Time and cost limits; high-level release map for initiation; risks; controls
teach.caption: Table 13.1. The project backlog, with its epics, is an output of the starting up workshop.

head: Topic
What it settles
rows: One to three key user groups, ranked first to third
Which option the project will pursue
Long-term outcomes; links to value and sustainability
Benefits and dis-benefits in small groups; tolerances
Timeline, tolerance, epics ranked with MoSCoW, dependencies
Costs, and the value the project brings
teach.caption: 13.2.4.1 and Table 13.2. The canvas workshop builds a shared foundation in line with organizational goals.

rows.label: Topics
values: Users, options, vision, benefits, risks, scope, cost, value
Roles, lessons review, initiation planning, risks, refine planning

rows.label: Key output
values: Initiation plan, project backlog with epics

teach.caption: Table 13.3: 'lessons review' gathers lessons from earlier initiatives in small groups; 'refine planning' updates the initiation plan and release map.
In starting up the PM defines who attends the project canvas and starting up workshops, sets dates and invites participants (13.2.3).

head: Activity
What the board does
rows: Approves the project brief and release map for initiation; informs stakeholders; lets the PM initiate
Approves the PID, confirms project tolerances, commits resources, authorizes delivery
Authorize a stage or exception plan
Reviews the updated project dashboard; approves the updated release map, or orders premature closure
Informal guidance and answers at any time, including on escalated issues
Compares PIDs, approves the end project report, ensures benefits reviews, confirms the updated canvas
teach.caption: Table 13.4.

teach.h: Agile enablement workshop, repeated each stage
teach.caption: Table 13.5. Review links earlier Agilometer results to agile values and transformation goals; identification adds adoption risks the Agilometer missed; assessment ranks by probability and impact; planning sets practical mitigation steps.

teach.h: Who is in the enablement workshop
teach.body: The agile enablement workshop belongs to directing a project. It is for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives, and it repeats the Agilometer assessment during initiation and later stages so that agile maturity and the risks of agile working are checked regularly. The first project Agilometer is built in the project initiation workshop; the enablement workshop keeps it alive.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares app
teach.body: Commercial director Bronwen Hale received the mandate, so as project executive she leads the project canvas workshop. The group ranks three user groups, app passengers first, and lists epics with MoSCoW. In the starting up workshop, Rhys Pengelly, Matteo Ricci (CPO), Gemma Lowther (senior supplier) and Bronwen create the project backlog. Rhys records the dependency on Coinbridge's fixed-price contract in the project brief. In stage 2 the board and agile lead Priyanka Desai hold the agile enablement workshop and add a threat the Agilometer missed: customer relations staff resisting the change.

teach.text: Traps: the executive leads the project canvas, not the PM or the CPO. The daily log starts in starting up, not initiation. The agile enablement workshop sits in directing and repeats the Agilometer; the agile transformation plan is not its output. Approving the release map for initiation is 'authorize initiation', while the PID is approved in 'authorize the project'.

items: Starting up: viable and worthwhile? Triggered by the mandate (an RFP can be one for a supplier).
Executive leads the canvas; PM, CPO, senior supplier and executive create the project backlog.
Project canvas workshop: users, options, vision, benefits, risks, scope, cost, value.
Starting up workshop: roles, lessons review, initiation planning, risk analysis, refine planning.
Directing: five authorize-or-direct activities; agile enablement workshop for the board and agile coaches.

summary: You can now place a starting up or directing event in the right activity and workshop topic, from user group definition to the agile enablement workshop. You can also say who should lead the project canvas and project backlog, and what the board approves at each directing decision.

A.q: Larkspur Rail's Fair Fares project is in starting up. In the project canvas workshop, the group discusses who will use the app, brainstorms possible user groups and ranks passengers who book in the app, disabled passengers and customer relations staff first to third. Which topic of the workshop is this?
A.why: User group definition brainstorms one to three key user groups and ranks them first to third, so the project has clear user priorities (Table 13.2).

whyNot.0: Benefits analysis works out benefits and dis-benefits in small groups and sets their tolerances; it does not rank user groups.
whyNot.2: Scope definition sets the timeline and tolerance and ranks epics with MoSCoW; it is not where user groups are chosen.
whyNot.3: Business value definition describes the value the project brings; ranking the people who use the product is user group definition.

A.q: Callowmere University's Student Support Hub project is in starting up. Project manager Jamal Hussain confirms the objectives, scope, exclusions and project tolerances, and notes that the hub depends on Northmere Systems upgrading its records interface and on the data protection officer's approval. Which activity is Jamal carrying out?
A.why: Assembling the project brief confirms objectives, outcomes, scope, exclusions and tolerances and records constraints, assumptions and dependencies on other projects or activities (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: Selecting the project approach evaluates delivery options and notes tailoring needs; it does not confirm tolerances and dependencies.
whyNot.1: Planning the initiation stage sets time and cost limits and a release map for initiation, not the project's scope and dependencies.
whyNot.2: The outline business case is the project canvas, led by the executive; the brief is where scope, tolerances and dependencies are pulled together.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's click and collect project has reached the end of stage 2. The project board reviews the updated project dashboard and the release map for stage 3, which project manager Patrick Dunne has updated, and approves it. Which directing activity is the board performing?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
Authorize the project, approving the PID
Give ongoing direction during the stage
A.why: In 'authorize a stage or exception plan' the board reviews the updated project dashboard and approves the updated release map, or tells the PM to close the project early (Table 13.4).

whyNot.1: Authorizing the project happens once, at the end of initiation, when the board approves the PID and confirms project tolerances.
whyNot.2: Ongoing direction is informal guidance at any time; approving the next stage's release map is a formal stage decision.
whyNot.3: Authorizing initiation approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, before stage 1 starts.

B.q: Easterholm County Council's Care Online project is in starting up. Sarah Pennington, director of adult social services, received the mandate and has been appointed project executive. Simon Archer is the project manager and Helen Crowther will be chief product owner. Who should lead the development of the project canvas from the mandate?
options: Helen Crowther, as chief product owner
Gita Bhatt, as the incoming agile coach
B.why: In 'prepare the outline business case' the project executive leads the development of the project canvas from the mandate (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: The PM leads the creation of the project backlog with the CPO, senior supplier and executive, but the executive leads the canvas.
whyNot.1: The CPO represents users and owns the project backlog; the canvas is the business justification, which the executive leads.
whyNot.3: The agile coach supports leaders with agile expertise; leading the business justification is the executive's job.

B.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's Smart Maintenance project is in stage 2. In the agile enablement workshop, the board has reviewed the Agilometer results. The group now brainstorms further threats to agile adoption that the sliders did not capture, such as engineers fearing the data will be used to monitor them. Which topic is this?
B.why: Risk identification brainstorms extra threats and opportunities for agile adoption that were not captured in the Agilometer, to build a complete list (Table 13.5).

whyNot.0: The Agilometer assessment review discusses risk areas already shown by earlier assessments and links them to agile values and transformation goals.
whyNot.2: Risk planning comes last and sets practical steps to carry out the mitigations.
whyNot.3: Risk assessment rates the probability and impact of risks already listed so they can be prioritized.

B.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group's Repairs Reimagined project is in starting up. In the starting up workshop, small groups collect what went well and badly on the association's earlier website project, its only agile work so far, and note how each point could affect this project. Which workshop topic is this?
B.why: The lessons review topic has small groups gather lessons from earlier projects or initiatives, add detail and outline their possible impact (Table 13.3).

whyNot.0: Risk analysis identifies, assesses and plans responses to threats and opportunities for initiation and the project, not past lessons.
whyNot.1: Refine planning updates the initiation stage plan and earlier documents, including the release map, after the other topics.
whyNot.2: Project roles aligns participants on the project management team and role descriptions.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's project initiation workshop produced the first project Agilometer. In stage 2, finance director Dominic Faraday proposes that the board stops holding agile enablement workshops, since the Agilometer has already been completed. Is this an appropriate application of the 'directing a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because the Agilometer is first assessed in initiation
Yes, because the board manages by exception through tolerances
No, because the board should reassess the Agilometer regularly
No, because each team should score the Agilometer every sprint
C.why: Directing includes the agile enablement workshop so that agile maturity and agile risks are assessed regularly, with Agilometer assessments in initiation and later stages (13.3.3, Table 13.5).

whyNot.0: It is true that the first project Agilometer comes from the project initiation workshop, but that is why later reassessment is needed, not a reason to stop.
whyNot.1: The board does manage by exception, but regular Agilometer review is part of how it directs an agile project.
whyNot.3: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: the regular reassessment is a board-level workshop, not a sprint-by-sprint team task.

C.q: Callowmere University's Student Support Hub project is in starting up. Project manager Jamal Hussain writes the whole project canvas himself from the mandate and then sends it to Professor Alison Greer, the project executive, to sign. Is this an appropriate application of the 'starting up a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because the PM manages starting up day to day
Yes, because the executive approves the project brief
No, because the canvas is first produced in initiation
No, because the executive should lead the project canvas
C.why: In 'prepare the outline business case' the executive leads the development of the project canvas from the mandate; the PM leads the project backlog with the CPO, senior supplier and executive (Table 13.1).

whyNot.0: The PM does run most starting up activities, but the canvas is the executive's to lead, so this does not justify Jamal writing it alone.
whyNot.1: The executive does approve the brief, but approving a document is not leading the canvas, which is what this activity asks.
whyNot.2: A canvas is started in starting up; initiation produces a more detailed one in 'prepare the full business case'.

C.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's starting up is complete. The project board reviews and approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, tells the stores that the project is being initiated, and allows Patrick Dunne to start initiation. Is this an appropriate application of the 'directing a project' process, and why?
options: Yes, because this is how the board authorizes initiation
Yes, because the board approves the PID at this point
No, because the release map is first drawn up in initiation
No, because stores are told once the project is authorized
C.why: In 'authorize initiation' the board approves the project brief and the release map for initiation, informs stakeholders and impacted sites, and authorizes the PM to initiate (Table 13.4).

whyNot.1: The PID does not exist yet; it is approved later, in 'authorize the project'.
whyNot.2: A high-level release map for initiation is produced in starting up, in 'plan the initiation stage'.
whyNot.3: Informing stakeholders and impacted sites is part of authorizing initiation, so telling the stores now is correct.

reteach.title: Opening a new restaurant
reteach.question: Before you sign a lease, how do you decide whether the idea is worth it, and who signs off each step?

blocks.body: An investor hands you a brief: open a family restaurant. First you check it is worth doing: who the diners are, what dishes they want, rough costs and risks. That is starting up. The investor then decides whether you may spend money on detailed plans, and later whether each phase can go ahead. That is directing. Every few months the investor and a mentor also check whether the new way of running the kitchen is taking hold.

head: Restaurant
PRINCE2 Agile
rows: One-page plan: diners, menu, cost, risk
Project canvas, led by the executive
Mentor and investor review the new kitchen culture

blocks.text: The chef does not write the investor's one-page case alone: the investor leads it. Likewise the executive leads the project canvas, and the PM leads the project backlog with the CPO, senior supplier and executive.

explain.body: The project mandate is whatever information triggers the project, provided by the responsible authority commissioning it. It may be a feasibility study or, in a supplier environment, a request for proposal. Starting up then asks whether the project is viable and worthwhile.

test.q: Coinbridge Payments receives a request for proposal from Larkspur Rail to build automatic card refunds. Coinbridge runs its own PRINCE2 Agile project to respond and deliver. What acts as the project mandate for Coinbridge's project?
test.why: The mandate is whatever information triggers the project; in a supplier environment a request for proposal can act as the mandate (13.2.1).

whyNot.0: Larkspur's project brief belongs to Larkspur's own project; it does not trigger Coinbridge's project.
whyNot.1: Coinbridge's canvas is produced in its starting up process, after the mandate has triggered it.
whyNot.2: A release map is a planning artifact produced later, not the trigger for the project.

explain.h: Benefits analysis in the canvas workshop
explain.body: In the project canvas workshop, benefits analysis has small groups brainstorm benefits and dis-benefits, share and discuss the results, and define tolerances. Ranking users, setting the vision and ranking epics are separate topics.

test.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group is in starting up. In the project canvas workshop, small groups list the expected gains from Repairs Reimagined, such as fewer second visits, and the downsides, such as extra training time, then agree tolerances for each. Which topic is this?
test.why: Benefits analysis brainstorms benefits and dis-benefits in small groups, discusses the results and defines tolerances (Table 13.2).

whyNot.1: Project vision definition explores long-term outcomes so the project aligns with business value and sustainability goals.
whyNot.2: Risk analysis covers uncertain events that could affect the project, not the expected gains and downsides of the outcome.
whyNot.3: Scope definition sets the timeline and tolerance and ranks epics with MoSCoW.

explain.body: Board members can give informal guidance or answer requests for advice at any time during the project. This is 'give ongoing direction', alongside responses to escalated issues, exception reports and the updated project dashboard.

test.q: Midway through stage 2 of Easterholm County Council's Care Online project, Simon Archer asks board member Joan Whitaker for informal advice on how to involve busy social workers. She replies the same day with suggestions. Which directing activity is this?
options: Authorize a stage or exception plan
test.why: Giving ongoing direction covers informal guidance and responses to requests for advice at any time during the project (Table 13.4).

whyNot.0: Authorizing a stage or exception plan is a formal decision on an updated release map, not informal advice.
whyNot.2: Authorizing the project is the one-off approval of the PID at the end of initiation.
whyNot.3: Authorizing initiation happens at the end of starting up, before stage 1.

explain.body: The agile enablement workshop is held for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives. It keeps agile maturity and the risks of agile adoption under regular review at board level.

test.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's project manager is inviting people to the agile enablement workshop for stage 3. Which group of participants does PRINCE2 Agile describe for this workshop?
options: The delivery teams with their POs and team coaches
The project manager, project support and the testers
The board, agile coaches and business representatives
The CPO, the product owners and a panel of end users
test.why: The agile enablement workshop is for the project board, agile coaches and organizational or business representatives (13.3.3).

whyNot.0: Delivery teams with their POs and team coaches attend team planning and retrospective workshops, not this board-level workshop.
whyNot.1: This group runs and supports delivery; the enablement workshop is a directing event for the board and coaches.
whyNot.3: The CPO, POs and users meet in workshops about the product; enablement reviews agile adoption risks at board level.
